name: Opus Picks-and-Shovels
strategy: Long diversified AI-infra suppliers (power + semi-cap + custom silicon) with a contained 15% 3x-semis leverage kicker and a small laggard short; leverage capped so the April-dip-style drawdown stays ~-14%, not -44%.

positions.thesis: Broad semis 1x, replacing SOXL's directional exposure without 3x volatility decay after the -50% month; captures a bounce cleanly.
GE Vernova power gen/grid — the datacenter power buildout leg, +8% over the drawdown month, the book's resilience anchor.
Semi cap-equipment; core picks-and-shovels supplier to every fab expansion, oversold in the pullback within a 3m uptrend.
Vertiv datacenter power/thermal; sold off -9% but structurally levered to AI compute density buildout.
Astera Labs AI connectivity silicon; picks-and-shovels for rack-scale interconnect scaling.
Arista datacenter networking; flat over the month (-0.3%) on durable AI back-end switching demand.
nVent electrical connection/protection; power-delivery hardware for datacenters, defensive infra leg.
Broadcom custom AI silicon and networking; diversified quality anchor of the compute stack.
Short the lowest-quality, margin-pressured AI server assembler; hedge that gained +14.6% this week and offsets long-semi beta.

reassessment_note: Week 1 desk (2026-07-18): Book held up well (-1.8% vs SMH -8.9%) on good construction, but the 15% SOXL 3x position decayed -50% in a month; de-lever SOXL into 1x SMH to cut volatility-decay tail risk while keeping the exact AI-infrastructure theme.
